### Description

Wi-Fi is a transmission technology of the wireless local area network (WLAN), based on the standard formulated by the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) for wireless local area networks: the 802.11 protocol.

WLAN follows the 802.11 protocol standard, from the earliest 802.11a/b/g, through 802.11n (Wi-Fi 4), 802.11ac (Wi-Fi 5), 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6/Wi-Fi 6e), to the latest 802.11be (Wi-Fi 7). Each evolution has brought a leap in data transmission rate.

### Frequency range and channels

The IEEE 802.11 protocol standard specifies the frequency bands and channels to be used, and each country formulates its own policy on which channels to use.

##### IEEE 802.11 protocol provisions for the 6GHz band:

Frequency range: 6GHz band, with a total of 1200MHz of spectrum used for WiFi 6E, ranging from 5.925GHz to 7.125GHz.

Main standard: an extended version based on IEEE 802.11ax (that is, WiFi 6), also known as WiFi 6E.

##### IEEE 802.11 protocol provisions for the 2.4GHz band:

Frequency range: 2.4GHz ~ 2.4835GHz; 14 channels, channel bandwidth 20M (the frequencies of multiple adjacent channels overlap). The frequency range of 22M shown below is because 2M is used as a mandatory isolation band and does not participate in data transmission.

##### IEEE 802.11 protocol provisions for the 5GHz band:

Frequency range: 5.150-5.250GHz, 5.250-5.350GHz, 5.470-5.725GHz, 5.745-5.825GHz; 201 channels in total, channel bandwidth 40M/80M/160M (selectable, the frequencies of multiple adjacent channels overlap).

##### China's provisions for the Wi-Fi 2.4GHz band:

Frequency range used: 2.4GHz ~ 2.4835GHz, with a total bandwidth of 83.5MHz. The corresponding channels are as follows:

The bandwidth of each channel is 22MHz, and the center frequency interval between adjacent channels is 5MHz. The frequencies of multiple adjacent channels overlap (for example, channel 1 overlaps in frequency with channels 2, 3, 4 and 5). Within the whole band, there are only 3 non-interfering channels (1, 6 and 11). Therefore, when using Wi-Fi devices in the 2.4GHz band, multiple devices that are close to each other should use different channels to prevent mutual interference.
